newsitem.title: UK: Euro Privatisation Trust picks M&G, Kleinwort.
newsitem.headline: Euro Privatisation Trust picks M&G, Kleinwort.

text.p: The board of the Kleinwort European Privatisation Investment Trust Plc is recommending shareholders opt to wind up their fund and invest in unit trusts managed by M&G and Kleinwort Benson Investment Management.

The board of the 500 million pound investment trust, which was launched in 1994 amid a wave of euphoria over European privatisations but failed to perform has chosen from 10 restructuring proposals but is still fighting off a hostile bid.

"The independent directors of KEPIT believe it is important to provide shareholders and warrantholders with the opportunity to retain an investment in a fund dedicated to privatised companies in Europe," chairman of the board Shane Ross said on Tuesday.

Ross said that proposals from M&G and KBIM would allow investors to choose between units in the Kleinwort Benson European Privatisation Trust, units in an existing European unit trust, the M&G's European and General Fund, or units in the Kleinwort Benson Money Market Trust, which can be held as an investment or redeemed to provide cash.
However, Ross again urged shareholders, who will vote on the board's proposals in November, to reject TR European Growth Fund's hostile bid.
"The independent directors believe the recommended proposal is clearly superior to TREG's offers...We urge you not to accept TREG's offers."
Warrantholders in KEPIT will be treated as if they hold three shares for every 10 warrants and will have the same choice as shareholders, Ross said.
At an extraordinary general meeting of shareholders in August, Ross said that expecations of the 500 million pound fund had been too high and "1994 was probably not the best time to launch".

Hostile bidder TR European, which reported a 37 percent rise in net asset value in its last financial year, has suggested an analogy between picking European privatisation stocks and having a fund of companies all beginning with the letter "B".

In the period running up to TR's bid, shares in KEPIT traded on a discount of between 12 and 20 percent to the underlying value of their investments, while TR European boasts is the best performing European investment trust over five years.
TR European has attacked unitisation as too expensive and it is offering a cash exit or the chance to invest in TR European.

It also notes that 18 million pounds in fees and commissions and eight million in management have been paid out since launch and that the underperformance of KEPIT relative to its nearest rival has cost investors 80 million pounds.

However, Shane Ross said that under the M&G and Kleinwort Benson proposals, some of KEPIT's assets would be transferred to the two trusts without incurring the dealing costs which any TR European liquidation of KEPIT would cause.

"M&G have identified approximately one third of KEPIT's securities which M&G European would be prepared to retain and KBIM and M&G have agreed how, depending on the level of elections for M&G Euro, a corresponding portion of these assets can be transferred to M&G European without KEPIT incurring dealing costs while protecting the interest of all KEPIT investors," Ross said.
He also said that two million pounds in management fees, which would be due to Kleinwort Benson Investment Management if the TREG bid went through, would not be payable.
